name: Izmir
tagline: Easy-going Aegean city with a great bazaar
summary: Turkey's third city is relaxed and liberal, with a seafront promenade and one of the country's best bazaars. One or two days here pair well with Ephesus, Alaçatı or Pergamon.
seasonNote: July and August are hot, when locals leave for the Çeşme peninsula; winters are mild and wet.
arrival: Adnan Menderes airport is 18 km south; the İZBAN suburban train reaches Alsancak in 30 minutes.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; use the metro, tram and the public ferries across the bay with an İzmirim card.
cashTip: Cards work nearly everywhere; carry small lira notes for the bazaar.
foodTip: Breakfast on boyoz pastry with a boiled egg; lunch on a kumru sandwich or söğüş; mussels stuffed with rice at night.
buyTip: Kemeraltı for spices, dried figs, leather and copper.
baseArea: Alsancak for restaurants and the seafront; Konak for the bazaar

connections.note: Regional trains from Basmane or the airport.

items.tip: Find Kızlarağası Hanı for Turkish coffee cooked in hot sand.

items.summary: A Hellenistic acropolis with the steepest theatre of the ancient world, above the town of Bergama.
items.expect: Two hours each way by bus; a cable car climbs to the acropolis.
items.tip: Add the Asklepion healing sanctuary if you have a car or taxi.

items.summary: Stalls and tiny shops selling Izmir's own snacks: boyoz, kumru, söğüş and şambali cake.
items.expect: Standing counters and a few stools.
items.tip: Try one of each over a morning, finishing with coffee at Kızlarağası Hanı.
